policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: The ASV question ends at "crucified?" with no clause answering to the added τῇ ἀληθείᾳ μὴ πείθεσθαι ("that ye should not obey the truth"); the longer reading would have to surface in English and does not.
ASV "before whose eyes Jesus Christ was openly set forth crucified" renders προεγράφη with no rendering of the added ἐν ὑμῖν ("among you"), which the ASV translates wherever it stands.
The variant is only the order of υἱοί and εἰσιν; "the same are sons of Abraham" renders either. The sole note is an alternative_rendering on "Know" and touches no reading.
ὅτι here is recitative before the quotation, and the ASV's "for it is written, Cursed is..." leaves nothing that would show whether it stood or was omitted.
"continueth not in all things" renders ἐμμένει πᾶσιν and ἐμμένει ἐν πᾶσιν alike; the English preposition is required by the verb either way.
ASV "He that doeth them shall live in them" has no noun for the added ἄνθρωπος; the longer reading is rendered "the man that doeth them," so the ASV's bare pronoun distinguishes the shorter text.
ASV "for it is written" is the natural rendering of both causal ὅτι γέγραπται and γέγραπται γάρ; the order of the connective leaves no English trace.
ASV renders the pair in order as "in Christ Jesus," matching Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ rather than the transposed Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, which the ASV would render "in Jesus Christ."
ASV "A covenant confirmed beforehand by God, the law..." passes straight from θεοῦ to the following clause with nothing answering to the added εἰς Χριστόν ("in Christ").
The variant is only whether ἔτη precedes or follows the numeral; "four hundred and thirty years" is the ASV's word order for either.
ἄχρις οὗ and ἄχρις ἂν are both rendered "till" before the subjunctive; "till the seed should come" does not distinguish them.
ASV "righteousness would have been of the law" renders ἐκ νόμου and excludes ἐν νόμῳ, which the ASV renders "in the law"; but it leaves the position of ἄν relative to ἐκ νόμου undetermined.
The variant is present συγκλειόμενοι against perfect συγκεκλεισμένοι; ASV "shut up unto the faith" is a participial phrase that carries neither tense distinctly.
πάντες and ἅπαντες are the same word with and without the intensive prefix and both are rendered "all"; "ye all are one man" does not distinguish them.
ASV sets "heirs according to promise" in apposition with no conjunction; the added καί is rendered "and heirs according to promise," and the ASV's asyndeton distinguishes the shorter reading.
